stem: The operations team at a retailer is rebuilding order processing to combine event-driven and microservice practices. They need order-status changes to reach interested services without polling, and they need any healthy service instance to be able to handle the next request from a given client. Which TWO design choices satisfy these two needs? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Publish order-status changes to an event bus for interested services to consume
Each service repeatedly querying a shared database table to check for new order-status rows
Have every service call the others synchronously and wait for a direct response before continuing
Externalize each service's session state to a shared data store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache
Each service instance caching its own local copy of a client's session data, refreshed from the database only when that instance restarts

rationale: Publishing order-status changes to an event bus lets interested services consume them as they happen, matching the first requirement. Externalizing session state to a shared data store is what lets any healthy instance pick up a client's next request, matching the second requirement. Having each service repeatedly query a shared database table for new rows is still polling: a real, workable technique, but the interested services are still the ones doing the asking, rather than reacting to a published event. Calling every service synchronously and waiting for a response creates a direct, blocking dependency between services instead of a published event, which is also the opposite of the polling-free requirement. Caching session data locally on each instance and only refreshing it from the database on restart still pins a client to whichever instance is holding the freshest copy of its session, so a different healthy instance cannot simply pick up the next request.
